He is now working to manufacture the Beerzooka in stainless steel, which he said would hold drinks cold for more than 12 hours. He runs Cruise Cup, which is entirely self-funded, from a 1,500-square-foot warehouse with two full-time employees, because he said you can only get so far working alone. His advice to young founders is to test as many ideas as possible, since social media and 3D printing are a free playground for testing ads and products.
Article Summary: Michael Satterlee, 18, of Clifton Park, New York, was a full-time high school student when he ran Solefully, a six-figure business that designs and 3D prints unique accessories for Crocs. He designed the Beerzooka, a patent-pending beer koozie, and prototyped it in a single day. He carried lessons from his first business into Cruise Cup, including how to structure a product on social media and build a Shopify store.

Article Title: In 2023, a Los Angeles man paid $50 for an old leather chair on Facebook Marketplace; months later, experts identified the rare 1930s design, and it sold for $107,950
Article Text:
Pic credit: Sotheby's, Instagram

An unassuming chair

Pic credt

Reaching out to Sotheby’s

Three minutes and a number that simply didn’t make sense

Justin Miller, a home design content creator from Los Angeles, spent half an hour scrolling through Facebook Marketplace. Most days, the search turned up nothing worth a second look. But in February 2023, he stumbled upon something unique: a chair. And that chair changed his year. He bought it for $50 and ended up selling it at a Sotheby’s auction on June 7 for $107,950 (including premiums).The listing was part of a yard sale at a home in Beverly Hills. The seller wanted $50 for a leather armchair. Miller, who was only 33 at the time, thought the colour of the leather was striking. He also liked the shape, which looked unusual to him. Although he knew little about furniture, he thought the chair was a bargain. “I’m not a furniture expert by any means. But I have a good eye, and I can tell when something is really unique,” Miller said in a TikTok post after finding the chair. That was enough for him to pay the asking price and drive the chair home.While he was arranging a collection time with the seller, he received a message that stuck with him. The seller told him that if he repaired the chair, it would be worth a lot.Miller took the comment seriously. He searched online and learned that the chair was truly unique.The oak and leather chair was made by Frits Henningsen, a Danish designer who worked in the 1930s. Only about 50 of these chairs were believed to have been made. Some similar pieces had already sold for six figures.Miller posted about his find on social media, and the comments were full of advice. Many viewers told him to contact an auction house, and he did. He reached out to Sotheby’s, and they agreed to restore the chair and sell it. They repaired the torn areas, conditioned the leather and tightened the fabric under the seat. The auction house gave the chair a pre-sale estimate of $30,000 to $50,000.The auction on June 7 lasted just under three minutes. Bids climbed past the estimate, and the chair sold for $85,000. With the buyer’s premium, the final total came to $107,950.Miller watched the sale live and recorded his reaction. The video went viral, garnering over four million views in a matter of hours. Carina Villinger, Sotheby’s head of 20th-century design, said the result set a record price for a chair by Henningsen. “We are absolutely delighted that Justin’s chair achieved this outstanding result. From the moment he contacted Sotheby’s to restore and sell his armchair, we’ve enjoyed learning about his discovery, which achieved a record price for this model by Frits Henningsen,” she told TODAY.Miller is delighted that his $50 chair earned him a fortune. He continues to hunt for bargains. “People always tell me they don’t find anything good on Facebook Marketplace. But they just aren’t looking hard enough.”
Article Summary: Justin Miller, a home design content creator from Los Angeles, found the chair at a yard sale in February 2023. He bought it for $50 and ended up selling it at a Sotheby's auction on June 7 for $107,950 (including premiums) The auction house gave the chair a pre-sale estimate of $30,000 to $50,000.

Article Title: In 2008, Michael Phelps used his $1 million Olympic bonus to start a foundation; by 2020, its programmes had reached more than 100,000 young people
Article Text:
In 2008, Michael Phelps used his $1 million Olympic bonus to start a foundation; by 2020, it had reached 100,000+ young people (Image Credit: Michael Phelps Foundation)

From Olympic success to a wider purpose

A swimming programme with lessons beyond the pool

Expanding the mission to mental health

Reaching children through partnerships

A legacy beyond medals

Winning eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics brought Michael Phelps worldwide recognition, but the swimmer also wanted to use his success to make a difference beyond the pool. He put his $1 million sponsor bonus towards establishing the Michael Phelps Foundation, an initiative focused on encouraging swimming, water safety and healthy living among young people. According to Boys & Girls Clubs of America, one of the foundation’s early efforts was a nationwide tour promoting his “Dream, Plan, Reach” message. Over the following years, its programmes expanded to include mental health education, reaching children through partnerships with youth organisations.Phelps had already made history in Beijing in 2008, winning eight gold medals at a single Olympic Games. But rather than keeping the entire sponsor bonus for himself, he used the $1 million to establish a foundation that could help more children discover swimming and learn skills that extend beyond sport. The Michael Phelps Foundation was established that year with a focus on water safety, youth swimming, wellness and goal-setting.Its early “Dream, Plan, Reach” initiative encouraged children to set ambitions and work towards them through consistent effort. The message reflected a familiar part of Phelps’ own sporting journey: success requires a clear goal, planning and the determination to keep going.The foundation began working with Boys & Girls Clubs of America, a network that provides programmes and support for young people in communities across the United States. Its early nationwide tour took Phelps’ message to club members, connecting his experience as an Olympic athlete with children who might not otherwise have access to structured swimming or development programmes.One of the foundation’s main initiatives is the “im” programme, developed with KidsHealth.org and the Michael Phelps Swim School. The name refers both to the individual medley, Phelps’ signature swimming event, and the words “I am”, reinforcing the idea of self-belief and personal growth. The programme combines swimming instruction and water-safety education with healthy living and goal-setting. Rather than concentrating only on athletic performance, it aims to help children become more comfortable in the water while developing confidence and habits that can support them in everyday life.According to Boys & Girls Clubs of America, the programme launched in 2010 at six clubs and expanded to 28 clubs by 2012. The foundation supports participating clubs through financial assistance, training, staff support, equipment, pool access and learning materials. These resources help organisations deliver lessons to children who may face barriers to swimming opportunities.Water safety is an important part of the initiative. Learning to swim can give children practical skills around pools and other bodies of water, while structured lessons can help them become more confident. The programme also uses goal-setting to encourage participants to recognise progress, work towards achievable targets and develop a sense of accomplishment.The foundation’s work later grew to include children’s emotional wellbeing. Its partnership with Nemours Children’s Health helped bring mental health education into its programmes, recognising that young people need support with emotional challenges as well as physical health and safety. During the COVID-19 pandemic, this aspect of the work became especially relevant. School closures, separation from friends and changes to familiar routines created difficulties for many children. In October 2021, Nemours Children’s Health and the Michael Phelps Foundation announced that their “IM Healthy” social-emotional learning programme had reached more than 50,000 children through 174 Boys & Girls Clubs of America.The programme drew on research and practices from areas including child development, psychology and paediatrics. Its lessons were designed to help children understand emotions, develop coping skills and recognise that it is normal not to feel okay all the time. The initiative extended the foundation’s original focus on healthy living by addressing the connection between emotional and physical wellbeing. The partnership also reflected Phelps’ growing willingness to speak publicly about mental health. By supporting conversations about emotions and resilience, the foundation sought to make such topics easier for children to discuss in supportive settings.The foundation’s reach has depended on working with organisations that already serve young people. Through Boys & Girls Clubs of America, Special Olympics International and other partners, its programmes have reached children and young people in different communities.A 2020 announcement reported that the foundation had provided learn-to-swim, healthy living and goal-setting programmes to more than 100,000 children and young adults around the world. The 2021 announcement from Nemours recorded a separate milestone for the “IM Healthy” curriculum, which reached more than 50,000 children through 174 Boys & Girls Clubs of America. These figures reflect different programme measures rather than a single cumulative total. Together, they illustrate how the foundation’s work expanded from swimming and goal-setting into emotional wellbeing education.Phelps’ Olympic achievements remain central to his public identity, but the foundation represents another part of his legacy. The $1 million bonus that followed his record-setting performance in Beijing helped establish a programme focused on skills children can use long after a swimming lesson ends.By combining water safety, healthy living, goal-setting and mental health education, the Michael Phelps Foundation has broadened its mission beyond sport. Its work shows how an athlete’s success can support initiatives that help young people develop confidence, resilience and safer, healthier habits.
Article Summary: Michael Phelps won eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. He used his $1 million sponsor bonus to set up the Michael Phelps Foundation. It focuses on swimming, water safety and healthy living among young people. By 2020, it has reached 100,000+ young people through its programmes.

Article Title: In 1972, three siblings gave Washington 590 acres on Squak Mountain instead of developing it; the land became the foundation of a state park
Article Text:
Representative Image of Squak Mountain’s serene wilderness with lush greenery and preserved natural landscapes ( AI Generrated Image)

How the Bullitt family acquired land on Squak Mountain

The conditions that protected the original 590 acres

Harvey Manning and the campaign to protect the foothills

Later land acquisitions expanded the park

On 17 June 1972, Ashley Ann Bullitt, Scott Bullitt and Jill Hamilton Bullitt transferred 590 acres of family land on Squak Mountain to Washington state for a wilderness park. Their gift followed decades of land purchases by their father, Stimson Bullitt, who had assembled a property of more than 600 acres and built a vacation cabin on the mountain. Rather than retain the land for private use or allow it to be developed, the siblings chose to protect it for public enjoyment under strict conditions. The donation laid the groundwork for Squak Mountain State Park, which later expanded through additional land purchases and conservation efforts. The history of the park reflects both the family’s decision and the work of local hikers, conservation advocates and public agencies that helped safeguard the surrounding foothills. Their decision shows how private generosity, paired with firm conditions and later public support, can secure a wild landscape for lasting public enjoyment instead of leaving it open to development.Stimson Bullitt began acquiring property on Squak Mountain during the 1940s, gradually bringing separate parcels together into a large family holding. He came from a prominent Pacific Northwest family associated with timber and broadcasting.In 1952, he built a 2-room vacation cabin on the mountain, providing a place for his family to spend time away from the city. The property eventually covered more than 600 acres around Squak Mountain’s 2,024-foot summit. In the early 1970s, the family trust transferred the land to 3 of Bullitt’s children: Ashley Ann, Scott and Jill Hamilton Bullitt. According to the history published by Washington State Parks, their father had reportedly outlined 3 possible uses for the property: the siblings could build homes for themselves, divide the land for development or donate it for a public park. They chose the third option. On 17 June 1972, they gave 590 acres to the Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission, with conditions intended to preserve the land’s wilderness character.The decision came during a period of change around Issaquah. Construction of Interstate 90 in the 1960s contributed to suburban growth in the area, while Squak Mountain had already experienced decades of resource extraction. Coal mining became an important part of Issaquah’s economy, and logging also altered parts of the mountain. The Issaquah Alps Trails Club’s history describes the area’s mining and logging past and traces how the Bullitt gift became the foundation of the state park. The mountain lies within the traditional territory of Coast Salish Indigenous peoples. Its geological history also predates the settlement and industrial activity that later shaped the region: the underlying rocks include sediments deposited in an ancient coastal environment.The Bullitt siblings did not simply donate the property for general recreation. The deed specified that the land should be managed as a wilderness park, excluding vehicles, horses, roads other than footpaths and man-made structures. Those restrictions distinguished the original donation from a conventional developed park. The family cabin did not survive for long after the land was transferred. According to the Issaquah Alps Trails Club’s account of the Bullitt family legacy, vandals had largely dismantled the 2-room building by the end of 1973. Its substantial stone fireplace remained, becoming a physical reminder of the cabin and the family’s connection to the mountain.A practical challenge remained: the donated property lacked a suitable connection to a public road for a formal trailhead and parking area. On 17 July 1984, the Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission purchased an additional 23 acres from North American Refractories Company. The land was part of the former Richmond-Harris Coal Mine property and provided access for visitors. This purchase was separate from the original Bullitt donation. The distinction matters because Squak Mountain State Park developed through several land transactions, while the wilderness conditions attached to the original 590 acres remained central to its identity.The creation of the park was followed by a wider conservation effort to protect the mountains surrounding Issaquah. Harvey Manning, a writer and wilderness advocate, helped popularise the name “Issaquah Alps” for the local foothills. Washington State Parks recounts that Manning turned to these nearby foothills when winter snow made his usual mountain destinations difficult to reach. Manning became an influential advocate for preserving the area and was a founding member and first president of the Issaquah Alps Trails Club. He praised the Bullitt donation as “the greatest act of environmental benevolence in local history”, according to the state parks history.Bill Longwell was another important figure in the effort. A hiker, teacher and musician, he helped survey routes and organise trail-building work. Manning gave him the nickname “Chief Ranger”. The club’s own history describes Longwell as one of its original members in 1979 and credits him with extensive work improving trails on Squak and Tiger Mountains. The club’s contribution continued beyond the park’s establishment. Its volunteers have helped maintain trails, remove invasive plants and support restoration work with Washington State Parks. Its 2025 account of Squak Mountain also records the organisation’s first group hike, led by Longwell on 6 June 1979.The original donation was only the beginning of Squak Mountain State Park’s development. In March 1992, the Trust for Public Land reached an agreement with the Grand Ridge Partnership to halt a proposed housing development beside the Bullitt property. The organisation purchased 17 building lots and secured an option on another 14, with the aim of transferring the land to the state. The acquisition was completed on 18 September 1995. Another expansion occurred through Washington’s Trust Land Transfer Program, authorised in 1989. The programme allows state trust land with significant ecological or social value but limited revenue potential to be transferred into public management. It also provides a mechanism for securing replacement land that can generate income for the relevant trust beneficiaries.Through this programme, 364 acres were added to Squak Mountain State Park in 1993 and 1994, according to Washington State Parks. Other acquisitions followed, bringing together land protected through the Bullitt family’s donation and later conservation efforts. Squak Mountain State Park therefore grew through a combination of private generosity, public investment and sustained local advocacy. The siblings’ 1972 gift established the original wilderness area; subsequent purchases and volunteer efforts helped protect a much larger landscape for future generations.
Article Summary: Stimson Bullitt began acquiring property on Squak Mountain during the 1940s. He built a 2-room vacation cabin on the mountain, providing a place for his family to spend time away from the city. In the early 1970s, the family trust transferred the land to 3 of Bullitt’s children: Ashley Ann, Scott and Jill Hamilton Bullitt. On 17 June 1972, they gave 590 acres to the Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission.

Article Title: George Washington spent much of his childhood at Ferry Farm; after Walmart bought the Virginia property in 1996, locals raised $2.2 million to save it and donated it to a nonprofit foundation
Article Text:
George Washington’s childhood home at Ferry Farm in Virginia was nearly replaced by a Walmart Supercenter.

How George Washington’s childhood home was saved

Residents launch a grassroots campaign

Walmart purchased the historic property in 1996, prompting residents to launch a campaign to save it.

How the community raised $2.2 million

Ferry Farm’s historical significance

Archaeologists discovered the foundation of Washington’s childhood home in 2008, and a replica opened to visitors in 2018.

Visitors can experience Washington’s childhood home

Thirty years ago, the historic site of George Washington’s childhood home in Virginia came close to being transformed into a Walmart Supercenter, until local residents rallied to save the property. Known as Ferry Farm, the site was purchased by the retail giant in 1996 for a proposed development, prompting concerns among community members about the loss of an important piece of American history. Residents organised campaigns, raised awareness and eventually collected $2.2 million to buy back the land. The property was subsequently donated to the George Washington Foundation, preserving the site where the first US president spent much of his childhood.Washington moved to Ferry Farm with his family when he was six years old. After his father died when he was 11, the young Washington inherited the farm and took on greater responsibilities within his family.The property played an important role in his formative years, introducing him to agriculture and land surveying. These skills later helped him establish a career as a surveyor in Culpeper County, Virginia, before he joined the militia and eventually became the first president of the United States.Despite its historical significance, Ferry Farm remained unprotected for years. In 1996, Walmart purchased the property with plans to build a Supercenter, according to WJLA. The development was initially welcomed by county officials, who were looking for ways to increase tax revenue.However, the proposal prompted a backlash among residents who believed that the historic land deserved protection.“And locals said, ‘Wait a minute, this isn't right,’” Heidi Bass, a Fredericksburg, Virginia, business owner, told WJLA.Among those who opposed the proposed development was Cessie Howell, who recalled refusing to accept that the historic site would be lost to commercial construction.“So many people would say, ‘It's a done deal.’ It's been signed, it's a done deal.’ And I just kept thinking, it just can't be a done deal. It can't be. George Washington, our hero, to have a Walmart next door,” Howell said.She and other advocates began organising a grassroots campaign to save the property. They advertised in newspapers, held community meetings and worked to draw attention to the site's historical importance.“We just started advertising in the paper and we had meetings here. It was right around George Washington's birthday, and people like you came and made it an important issue,” Howell told WJLA.She also credited television coverage with helping spread awareness of the campaign beyond the local community.“Had we not had stations like your station, we would not be where we are today because it spread across the United States,” she said.As opposition to the Walmart development gained momentum, residents and supporters raised $2.2 million to buy back the property. Walmart ultimately accepted the offer, allowing the land to be transferred to the Kenmore Foundation, now known as the George Washington Foundation.The successful campaign became an example of how community action and public awareness can help preserve historically significant places threatened by commercial development.Reflecting on the outcome, Howell expressed gratitude to the people who contributed to the effort.“I'm just thankful that all these people came together and saved it,” she said.Ferry Farm was designated a National Historic Landmark in 2000, four years after the campaign to save it began. The designation recognises the site's historical importance and raises its profile, although it does not automatically prevent commercial development.For historians and archaeologists, the property offers an opportunity to understand Washington's early life beyond the familiar story of his military and political achievements.The oldest remaining building on the property is a small shed dating to the 1870s. In 2008, archaeologists discovered the structural foundation of the house where Washington spent his childhood. A replica of the home was completed a decade later and opened to the public in 2018.The reconstructed house allows visitors to explore the domestic environment in which Washington grew up and learn about the everyday experiences that shaped his early years.Today, Ferry Farm operates as a historic attraction where visitors can explore the reconstructed house and learn about life during Washington's childhood.Allison Burgess, director of education at the George Washington Foundation, said the site offers an interactive experience designed to help visitors connect with history.“Ferry Farm is one of the most family friendly museums you're going to find in the area. When you go in the Washington house, you don't have to worry about saying, ‘please don't touch that.’ You're allowed to touch anything because we want you to interact with the entire experience in the house,” Burgess said.She explained that visitors are encouraged to sit on the beds and chairs, examine the table settings and engage with the furnishings rather than simply observing them from a distance.“We want you to sit on the bed and test out the rope beds. We want you to sit in the chairs, pull up a chair to the dining room table. Look at the silverware on the tables. It's a very interactive experience,” she added.
Article Summary: Walmart purchased the historic property in 1996, prompting residents to launch a campaign to save it. Residents organised campaigns, raised awareness and eventually collected $2.2 million to buy back the land. Property was subsequently donated to the George Washington Foundation, preserving the site where the first US president spent much of his childhood.

Article Title: New rule for H-1B again? Visa extensions will be treated as fresh cases; asylum seekers and H-4 visa holders will also be affected
Article Text:
H-1B visa extension applications will be treated as fresh cases and will draw more scrutiny and questions.

What is the new rule?

Again a new rule dropped from the Department of Homeland Security that will concern H-1B visa holders. But the scope of the new rule will be far greater than just H-1Bs. It will impact anyone with a work authorization in the US as the DHS issued a rule eliminating a grace period for immigrants whose work authorization expires while renewal applications are still pending.The measure released Tuesday makes permanent an interim final rule DHS issued last year doing away with a 540-day automatic extension period adopted under the Biden administration. The agency said the change, which affects asylum seekers as well as spouses of H-1B specialty occupation workers, would allow for more frequent vetting of applicants, Bloomberg reported.The extension window was designed to ensure immigrant workers aren’t pushed out of jobs because of processing delays at US Citizenship and Immigration Services.The final rule will take effect after it’s published in the Federal Register on October 14 with a 30-day public comment period.As of June 30, more than 432,000 work permit renewal applications were pending at USCIS for six months, including more than 91,000 for more than a year and a half. Foreign workers aren’t eligible to re-up the documents until 180 days before their expiration date, the Bloomberg report said. A group of H-4 visa holders sued DHS in January, arguing the policy change violated the Administrative Procedure Act.A California judge last month enjoined the interim final rule for those plaintiffs, finding it didn’t follow procedural requirements or acknowledge the reliance interests of plaintiffs, the report added.Extensions of work authorizations of H-1Bs and H-4s now do not attract the same scrutiny as these people have already been working and if they are applying for an extension with the same employers and the same job, the USCIS does not treat it as a fresh case but now it will.This means there will be more denials, more documentation, more RFEs. USCIS could reexamine whether the employee qualifies for the position and whether the job meets H-1B requirements. Employers and employees may face additional requests for evidence and documentation.
Article Summary: H-1B visa extension applications will be treated as fresh cases and will draw more scrutiny and questions. The final rule will take effect after it’s published in the Federal Register on October 14 with a 30-day public comment period. A group of H-4 visa holders sued DHS in January, arguing the policy change violated the Administrative Procedure Act.

Article Title: 6 killed, several injured as passenger train derails in Pakistan's Punjab
Article Text:
Train travelling from Karachi to Peshawar derails in Pakistan (Representative image) (PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority to prevent train accidents? Improving railway tracks Upgrading safety systems Regular maintenance and inspections 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

At least six people were killed and several others injured after a passenger train derailed in Pakistan's Punjab province early Tuesday, Pakistan-based Geo News reported.The Rehman Baba Express, travelling from the southern port city of Karachi to the northwestern city of Peshawar, derailed in Sher Shah, Punjab province, news agency AP reported, citing Pakistan Railways spokesperson Kaleem Akhtar.The injured were taken to Nishtar Hospital in Multan for treatment, while rescue teams continued operations at the accident site.The accident took place at around 5.15am, according to Geo News.Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed grief over the deaths in separate statements and directed authorities to ensure the best possible medical care for the injured.Train accidents are relatively common in Pakistan, where the railway system has suffered from decades of underinvestment, outdated tracks and ageing signalling systems.In 2023, 10 carriages of a passenger train derailed in southern Pakistan, killing 30 people and injuring more than 90 others.
Article Summary: Passenger train travelling from Karachi to Peshawar derails in Pakistan. At least six people killed and several others injured in Sher Shah, Punjab province. Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif express grief over the deaths.

Article Title: 2 Pakistan army pilots killed as training aircraft crashes near Balochistan's Quetta
Article Text:
2 Pakistan army pilots killed (IANS photo)

Two Pakistan army pilots were killed after a Mushshak training aircraft crashed near Balochistan's Quetta on Monday due to a technical fault, as Dawn reported, citing the ISPR, the official media wing of the Pakistan armed forces.The Pakistan army identified the deceased as Major Husnain Shehzad Humayun, an instructor, and Captain Abdul Samad, a trainee pilot.The aircraft crashed near Nawan Killi in Quetta.In June, a Mi-17 helicopter belonging to the Pakistan army's aviation wing crashed during take-off near Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), reportedly due to a technical fault.All personnel on board were killed. The ISPR said rescue and recovery teams were rushed to the site and an inquiry was ordered to determine the cause of the crash, Dawn reported.In September last year, five crew members died when a Pakistan army helicopter crashed in the Diamer district of Pakistan-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan (PoGB). The ISPR said the helicopter had encountered a technical fault.In August 2025, five crew members were also killed when a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government helicopter carrying flood relief supplies crashed in a tribal district, Pakistan-based daily The Express Tribune reported.
Article Summary: Pakistan army identifies the deceased as Major Husnain Shehzad Humayun, an instructor, and Captain Abdul Samad, a trainee pilot. The aircraft crashed near Nawan Killi in Quetta. In June, a Mi-17 helicopter belonging to the Pakistan army's aviation wing crashed during take-off in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

Article Title: Laiba Ijaz suicide: Pakistan gold medalist commits suicide after visa scam; suspect on 5-day remand
Article Text:
20-year-old physics gold medallist committed suicide after allegedly being scammed of Pakistani Rs 93 lakh over promise of getting an admission in Harvard

Family alleges loss of Pakistani Rs 9.3 million

What FIR alleges

A 20-year-old Pakistani student, Laiba Ijaz, died by suicide on October 9 after allegedly being defrauded of millions of rupees by an agent who promised to secure her admission to Harvard University, a scholarship and a US visa. An Islamabad court on Monday granted police five days of physical remand of the main accused, Muhammad Noman, in connection with the case, Voice PK reported.Judicial magistrate Zunaira Zafar passed the order after police produced Noman in court with his face covered. Police had sought 10 days of remand to investigate his alleged role, verify evidence and examine witness statements.Pakistan's Senate Standing Committee on Human Rights has also sought a detailed inquiry into Laiba's death and the alleged fraud. According to police reporting, the committee will meet on October 15. Islamabad's inspector general of police, the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) director general and the Higher Education Commission chairman have been directed to attend.The committee has sought details of the case registration, the suspect's arrest and the investigation so far. It has also asked authorities to report on steps taken to cancel the licence of the educational consultant accused of issuing fake documents.According to local reports, Laiba was found hanging from a tree in Islamabad's Sector G-10 on Friday, October 9. Police said she had paid an agent Rs 5 million to arrange her travel to the United States but was later given fake documents.Laiba had left home around 2pm, telling her mother she would return shortly. When she failed to come back, her family searched for her and tracked her location using her mobile phone. They found her body and informed the police, who took it to a hospital.The Media Line reported that Laiba was a physics gold medallist and scholarship holder who aspired to become a scientist and study at Harvard. Her family allegedly lost Rs 9.3 million, approximately $34,000, to those promising her admission, a scholarship and a US visa.Her father had sold milk and yoghurt on Islamabad's streets since 1994 to support his family's education. To finance Laiba's studies abroad, he reportedly sold land intended for the family's home, while her mother pawned her jewellery. Laiba had also declined a scholarship in Saudi Arabia because she wanted to pursue her ambitions in the United States.Shortly before her death, Laiba called her brother-in-law and said, "Don't tell my father about the fraud committed against me; otherwise, he will die."Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an investigation into the case.According to the police FIR, Laiba's father said the family had met Noman around six to seven months before her death. Noman allegedly introduced himself as a senior official in Islamabad and offered to arrange a US study visa for Laiba for Rs 9.3 million.The father alleged that he paid Rs 2.1 million in cash to Noman at G-10 Markaz in the presence of witnesses. Laiba transferred another Rs 2.9 million through her mobile and bank accounts, according to the complaint.Noman allegedly supplied documents that later turned out to be fake. He also reportedly presented a forged receipt showing a transfer of $20,000 into Laiba's bank account to help prepare a bank statement. The father said Noman stopped answering his calls after the family questioned him about the documents.The father also accused a woman identified as Fatima Sarwar, alias Aiza, of involvement in the alleged fraud. She reportedly contacted Laiba and demanded more money. He said Laiba had been in severe distress for five to six days before her death and blamed Noman and Aiza for her suffering.A separate complaint lodged by Laiba's uncle, Amjad Rehman, with the FIA's Anti-Human Trafficking Circle named Noman and Aiza as accused in an alleged conspiracy to defraud the family of Rs 9.3 million. The complaint alleged that Rs 2.9 million was transferred to Noman's bank account, while the remaining amount was paid in cash at a shop in Gulistan Plaza, G-10 Markaz.Senior lawyer Raja Naveed Kiyani said police and the FIA could register separate FIRs over the same incident. He explained that the FIA could pursue its own investigation and seek Noman's custody through the court after he was transferred from police custody to judicial remand.The allegations against Noman and Aiza are yet to be established in court. The case has also highlighted concerns over fraudulent educational consultants who target Pakistani students seeking admission and scholarships abroad.
Article Summary: 20-year-old physics gold medallist committed suicide after allegedly being scammed of Pakistani Rs 93 lakh over promise of getting an admission in Harvard. An Islamabad court on Monday granted police five days of physical remand of the main accused, Muhammad Noman, in connection with the case.

Article Title: Imran Khan’s stronghold in crisis: What's happening after emergency rule in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Article Text:
Supporters of imprisoned former Pak PM Imran Khan's at protest to condemn state of emergency in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province

Why governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa apex committee vows continued operations

Imran Khan’s son condemns emergency

Petition challenges emergency and governor’s rule in court

Roadblocks, arrests and school closures

Why Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is important to Imran Khan’s PTI

What now

Pakistan’s political confrontation over jailed former prime minister Imran Khan has escalated after the federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, suspending the authority of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial administration. The move, announced on Sunday, brings one of the party’s most important political strongholds under federal control and has intensified tensions between the government led by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Khan’s supporters.President Asif Ali Zardari approved the measures under Articles 232(1) and 234(1) of Pakistan’s Constitution, citing a deteriorating security situation. Islamabad has accused the provincial government of failing to cooperate in the fight against terrorism, while the PTI has called the move an attempt to undermine its electoral mandate. A petition challenging the measures was filed in the Peshawar high court on Monday. Meanwhile, arrests, roadblocks, school closures and examination postponements have disrupted life in several districts as the authorities tighten security.The federal government announced emergency and governor’s rule after a cabinet meeting on Sunday reviewed the security situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which borders Afghanistan and has faced a persistent militant threat.In a statement, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s office said the cabinet had examined the deteriorating law and order situation and the provincial government’s “deliberate indifference in the war against terrorism”.Islamabad has accused the PTI-led administration of failing to take adequate action against militants and of not cooperating with federal authorities on security policy. Federal ministers have also alleged a “nexus” between the provincial government and terrorist groups, a charge the PTI disputes.Militants linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which shares an ideological affinity with the Afghan Taliban, have carried out attacks against security personnel and civilians in Pakistan. The federal government has argued that a coordinated response is necessary to counter the threat.The PTI, however, says it has been excluded from decisions concerning security in its own province. It has opposed military operations on its territory and called for a review of the counterterrorism strategy, including Islamabad’s approach to engagement with the Afghan Taliban.The disagreement contributed to the breakdown of talks between the federal government and PTI representatives on October 3.Under governor’s rule, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has taken charge of running the province. The federal government has also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power.The federal government has cited worsening law and order as the basis for its intervention. However, figures from the Islamabad-based Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS), cited in the morning report, suggest the trend in reported deaths in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was not identical to the national picture.Civilian and security personnel deaths in the province reportedly totalled 485 in the first nine months of 2026, a decline of 16 per cent from the same period in 2025. Across Pakistan, such deaths rose by 9 per cent over the corresponding period, according to the think-tank.The figures provide a counterpoint to the federal government’s account of the province’s security situation, but they do not, by themselves, establish whether the provincial administration adequately addressed militant activity or explain the reasons behind the change in fatalities.The new administration has pledged to strengthen the police and the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), increase operational resources and continue intelligence-based operations against militants.The provincial Apex Committee held its first meeting under the new arrangement on Monday at the Governor House in Peshawar. It was co-chaired by Kundi and interior minister Mohsin Naqvi and attended by senior civil and military officials, including the Peshawar Corps Commander, chief secretary and inspector general of police.Kundi said tackling terrorism would be the administration’s immediate priority, pointing to what he described as a lack of coordination in counterterrorism efforts. “We can sacrifice our development, but never security,” he said, adding that the administration would “fulfil the demands of the Counter-Terrorism Department and police”, reported Dawn.He also promised a more results-oriented approach. “We have to show the difference,” Kundi said, adding that the administration would “work 24/7”.The governor highlighted the impact of militancy on daily life in districts such as Dera Ismail Khan, Tank and Waziristan, saying residents faced restrictions on their freedom to live and travel. He called for restoring normal movement and expressed hope that the new administration would be remembered for bringing peace to the province.Naqvi, meanwhile, accused the previous provincial government of failing to lead the fight against terrorism despite repeated requests from the Centre. “Today is the first time I can proudly say that the federal and the provincial governments are on the same page,” he said.Naqvi argued that security operations could not succeed without political leadership. “But any war, no matter how many resources you have, cannot be won until the government leads it,” he said.He cautioned that the situation would not change overnight but called on the governor, police, administration and federal government to work together.The committee resolved to continue intelligence-based operations and use all available resources to improve law and order. It also decided to strengthen the police and CTD with modern equipment, vehicles, armoured vehicles, weapons and additional personnel.Alongside security, the committee pledged to address public grievances, improve access to basic services and promote development in underdeveloped and conflict-affected areas.Kasim Khan, son of the jailed former prime minister, condemned the emergency and governor’s rule, accusing Army Chief Asim Munir of using terrorism as a justification for another military operation in Pashtun areas.In a post on X, Kasim linked the measures to protests demanding his father’s release and alleged that the authorities were seeking to consolidate power through military action.“Pakistan belongs to its people, not its military,” he wrote.Kasim called for the restoration of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s democratic mandate and the immediate release of his father, detained family members, PTI representatives and other political prisoners. He also demanded that the right to protest be respected.The emergency was imposed as the PTI was holding a long march led by provincial Chief Minister Sohail Afridi. The march called for Imran Khan’s release and access to medical treatment for him, while also opposing military operations that the party says have caused civilian deaths and damage.Afridi and seven other PTI leaders were taken into protective custody, according to reports. Afridi had vowed to continue the march before the provincial government’s powers were suspended, PTI reported.“There is no option other than accepting our demands,” Afridi said in a post on X before the takeover.“We will not back down,” he added. “Our long march will continue until the demands are met, in accordance with the law. Here, only Imran Khan’s policy will prevail.”The PTI has accused the federal government of using security concerns to weaken the party and undermine the elected provincial administration.“The arrest of chief minister Sohail Afridi and Junaid Akbar has exposed the political nature of the government’s actions,” PTI spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram said in a statement.“These measures are not directed at addressing security challenges; they are intended to weaken PTI, undermine the elected government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and disregard the democratic will of its people,” he alleged.The status of Junaid Akbar, a member of parliament and president of the PTI’s provincial chapter, requires separate confirmation before any arrest claim is treated as established.The federal government’s decision faced a legal challenge on Monday, with a petition filed in the Peshawar High Court less than 24 hours after the measures were introduced.Filed by Advocate Salman, the petition names President Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Governor Kundi as respondents. It argues that the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule is “unconstitutional, illegal and motivated by mala fide intentions”.The petitioner has also alleged that the measures violate fundamental rights and undermine the democratic mandate of the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.Separately, opposition leaders met in Islamabad on Monday to discuss the emergency and its aftermath. Those present included PTI chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai and PTI secretary general Barrister Salman Akram Raja. The participants also discussed challenging the measures in court.The legal challenge adds another front to the confrontation, with the province’s administrative status now under scrutiny alongside the government’s security justification.The impact of the emergency has varied across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with heightened security deployments, transport restrictions, school closures and arrests reported in several districts.In Peshawar, police remained deployed along major roads, while shipping containers blocked several routes, particularly around the cantonment area. Entry and exit points to Peshawar Cantt were closed, and access to areas including Khyber Road, parts of University Road and GT Road near Pir Zakori was restricted. Commuters were diverted to alternative routes.Traffic was relatively light on parts of the city’s road network on Monday afternoon. Educational institutions across the provincial capital remained closed. Internet and cellular services, which had been disrupted, were reported to have been fully restored in Peshawar, according to Dawn News.In Mardan, government and private schools, colleges and universities were shut, and examinations scheduled for the day were cancelled. Several education boards postponed secondary school examinations, including in Bannu, North Waziristan, Dera Ismail Khan and Lakki Marwat. Fresh dates are to be announced.In Charsadda, police confirmed that 15 PTI workers had been arrested. In Shangla, more than two dozen party workers had been taken into custody, according to the district police chief. Authorities also imposed Section 144, prohibiting gatherings, and ordered intensified patrolling and checks at district entry and exit points.Containers were placed to block the Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway near Swabi, where internet and mobile services remained suspended. In Bannu, road restrictions were reported near the cantonment area.The situation was comparatively calm in parts of Khyber district. A PTI demonstration in Bara was dispersed by police, but roads, including the main Peshawar-Torkham Highway, remained open.In Lower South Waziristan, schools and colleges were closed, but markets and routine commercial activities continued. No major disruption to commercial activity or significant protests were reported there.Tank district imposed a one-month ban on pillion riding from October 10 to November 9 under Section 144, citing security concerns.The differing conditions across districts underline the uneven impact of the emergency. While restrictions have affected transport, education and political activity in several areas, routine life has continued in others.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been a key political base for Imran Khan’s PTI, which has governed the province since 2013. The party remained a major force in the 2024 elections despite Khan’s imprisonment and the difficulties faced by its candidates.Khan, a former Pakistan cricket captain who served as prime minister from 2018 to 2022, was removed from office through a parliamentary no-confidence vote. He has been in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi since 2023 and faces more than 100 cases, including corruption and charges related to inciting violence.Candidates backed by Khan won the largest number of seats in the National Assembly in the 2024 elections, but the party was kept out of federal power as other political parties formed the government.The takeover of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa therefore carries significance beyond the change in provincial administration. It places a crucial PTI-governed province under a federal arrangement at a time when the party is mobilising supporters for Khan’s release and challenging Islamabad’s counterterrorism policy.The PTI maintains that the federal government’s actions undermine the provincial electorate’s mandate. Islamabad, in turn, argues that the security situation requires decisive intervention and closer coordination between the provincial and federal authorities.The imposition of governor’s rule has sharpened the divide between the PML-N-led federal government and the PTI, which has governed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for more than a decade. Their dispute centres on responsibility for worsening militancy, the scope of military operations and the provincial administration’s role in security policymaking.The Centre maintains that the provincial government failed to adequately support counterterrorism efforts. The PTI says it was excluded from decisions concerning its own province and argues that the takeover undermines the democratic mandate of its voters.With the emergency facing a legal challenge, PTI leaders in custody and security restrictions disrupting parts of the province, the confrontation is now unfolding on political, judicial and security fronts. The federal government has pledged a more coordinated campaign against terrorism, while the opposition is demanding the restoration of the province’s elected administration.
Article Summary: The federal government has imposed emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, suspending the authority of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial administration. Islamabad has accused the provincial government of failing to cooperate in the fight against terrorism. A petition challenging the measures was filed in the Peshawar high court on Monday.

Article Title: Why did Pakistan declare Emergency in Imran Khan's bastion Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Article Text:
Emergency in Imran Khan’s bastion: Why Shehbaz Sharif’s govt took control of KP

PTI leaders arrested after emergency announcement

Imran Khan’s stronghold at the centre of political battle

Pakistan's political battle with jailed former prime minister Imran Khan has taken a sharp turn, with the Shehbaz Sharif government suspending his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led administration in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and imposing governor's rule in the province.The move brings one of Imran Khan's strongest political strongholds under direct control of the Shehbaz Sharif-led government, further deepening the confrontation between the military-backed government and PTI.Amid growing insecurities within the Shehbaz Sharif-Asim Munir duo, Imran Khan’s party has lost control of a province with around 40 million people, turning the region into the latest flashpoint in Pakistan’s political unrest.Thousands of people have taken to the streets in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa since early October, demanding Imran Khan’s release and protesting the military’s counter-insurgency operations along the border with Afghanistan.The Pakistan government has defended the move, citing the worsening law and order situation and accusing the provincial administration of failing to act against terrorism. Militants linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), an ideological ally of the Afghan Taliban, have killed thousands of security personnel and civilians in recent years.“The Cabinet took a detailed review of the deteriorating law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the circumstances arising from the provincial government’s deliberate indifference in the war against terrorism,” the office of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said in a statement.However, figures compiled by the Islamabad-based Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS) paint a different picture of the security situation in the province, as Financial Times reported.Civilian and security personnel deaths in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa stood at 485 in the first nine months of 2026, down 16% from the same period in 2025. Across Pakistan, such deaths rose by 9%, according to the think-tank.Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari approved the emergency on the prime minister’s advice. His office cited a “failure of negotiations” between the Pakistan government and PTI leaders in the province.Under governor’s rule, the governor, who is appointed by the Pakistan government, takes over the province’s administration. Pakistan’s interior ministry said the army would deploy personnel to help run the province and protect public property and government installations.Talal Chaudhry, junior interior minister, told the Financial Times that the move was a “routine measure” intended to help provincial authorities carry out their responsibilities, particularly in the fight against terrorism.The political confrontation intensified soon after the announcement, with reports emerging that senior PTI leaders had been arrested.An account on X associated with Junaid Akbar, a member of parliament and president of PTI’s provincial chapter, said he and provincial chief minister Sohail Afridi had been taken into custody.Afridi, 37, had been leading a long march across the province in support of Khan and against military operations that PTI claims have caused civilian deaths and damage. He is the youngest-ever chief minister of Pakistan and comes from the tribal belt bordering Afghanistan.Just hours before his government was suspended, Afridi had vowed to continue the march until the protesters’ demands were met.“There is no option other than accepting our demands,” Afridi said in a post on X.“We will not back down,” he said. “Our long march will continue until the demands are met, in accordance with the law. Here, only Imran Khan’s policy will prevail.”Pakistan’s interior ministry and armed forces did not respond to requests for comment, the Financial Times reported.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been a key political base for Imran Khan's PTI, which has governed the province since 2013. The party won more than 60% of the seats in the provincial assembly in the 2024 elections, two years after Khan was removed as prime minister through a parliamentary no-confidence vote.The former World Cup-winning cricket captain continues to be widely regarded as Pakistan’s most popular politician. Candidates backed by him won the largest number of seats in the national assembly in 2024.However, they were kept out of power as the military and the country’s two dominant dynastic political parties shaped the post-election arrangement, according to the Financial Times.The FT also cited analysts as saying PTI would comfortably win a competitive general election.PTI has accused the Shehbaz Sharif government of using security concerns as a pretext to remove its elected administration in the province.“The arrest of chief minister Sohail Afridi and Junaid Akbar has exposed the political nature of the government’s actions,” PTI spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram said in a statement.“These measures are not directed at addressing security challenges; they are intended to weaken PTI, undermine the elected government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and disregard the democratic will of its people.”
Article Summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is one of Imran Khan's strongest political strongholds. Shehbaz Sharif-led government has imposed governor's rule in the province. Reports emerge that senior PTI leaders have been arrested. Pakistan government has defended the move, citing the worsening law and order situation.

Article Title: Pak crisis: Shehbaz govt declares emergency, ends Imran Khan's party's rule in KPK
Article Text:
PTI has been mobilising supporters to pressure the federal government over Khan's imprisonment

Terrorism, law and order cited

PTI protests, warns of bloodshed

Pakistan on Sunday declared an emergency in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), suspending the provincial government led by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party amid deteriorating law and order and a growing confrontation with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government.President Asif Ali Zardari issued the proclamation under Articles 232(1) and 234(1) of the Constitution, citing rising terrorist attacks and a breakdown of constitutional machinery in the province. The move strips the elected provincial administration of its powers, with the chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general required to vacate their offices.Following the announcement the Pak government order the deployment of army in the province.The decision comes as thousands of PTI supporters march towards Islamabad, demanding Khan's release and access to medical treatment for the former prime minister, who has been in prison since 2023 on corruption and other charges. The party has described the cases against him as politically motivated. The emergency also follows failed negotiations between PTI and the federal government over the planned protest.The presidential declaration said the emergency had been imposed because of the grave security situation and the provincial government's alleged failure to tackle militancy.“The extraordinary intensity of terrorist incidents poses serious threats to the lives and property of the public,” the declaration stated.PTI has been mobilising supporters to pressure the federal government over Khan's imprisonment. KPK chief minister Sohail Afridi is leading the protest march, which began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 and has passed through several districts.The party had initially planned to take the march to Islamabad for a sit-in, but authorities have erected roadblocks using shipping containers at entry points to the capital and other locations. Two rounds of talks between PTI and the government failed to break the deadlock.Zulfikar Bukhari, a close Khan aide and PTI spokesman, called the emergency a “ridiculous decision”, saying KPK had the country's “only legitimately elected government”.“This will only lead to further bloodshed, instability and collateral damage,” he said, adding that there had always been room for talks but the decision showed negotiations were never the government's intention.Previous protests by Khan's supporters have turned violent, with security personnel and civilians killed during demonstrations in 2024.
Article Summary: President Asif Ali Zardari declares emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Suspends provincial government led by Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party. Decision comes as thousands of PTI supporters march towards Islamabad, demanding Khan's release.

Article Title: ‘No contact, no update’: Imran Khan’s son says father silent for 6 months, aunts remain ‘abducted’
Article Text:
Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest

Kasim says protests will continue

Sisters detained ahead of PTI protest

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan’s son Kasim Khan has claimed that his three aunts remain “abducted” by Pakistani authorities, saying their family and lawyers have received no information about their condition or the reasons for their detention. He also said he and his brother have had no contact with their father for more than six months.Kasim Khan made the remarks on Thursday, weeks after his aunts Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned September 27 protest and march to Islamabad.The demonstrations were called to demand updates on Imran Khan's health and his release from Adiala Jail, where the former prime minister has been incarcerated since August 2023.In a post on X, Kasim Khan linked the continued detention of his aunts with the lack of contact with his father."Currently, my Aunties are still abducted. Family and lawyers have received no update on how they are, nor why they are incarcerated. Concerning my father, there is complete silence. My brother and I have had no contact with him for more than six months. We do not even know the true state of his health," the post read.Kasim Khan also referred to protests being held in Pakistan over his father's imprisonment, saying people were continuing to demand justice and the right to be heard."Meanwhile, thousands of Pakistanis are peacefully taking to the streets to protest against his illegal and politically motivated imprisonment. However, the people of Pakistan have not given up. No barricade, intimidation or repression can muzzle the people’s demand for justice and their democratic right to be heard. There can be no lasting peace or stability while their democratic will is suppressed and their chosen leader remains behind bars,” Kasim Khan added.His remarks came a day after the families of the three detained sisters approached the Lahore High Court seeking permission for relatives and lawyers to meet them.According to Dawn, Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar filed two civil miscellaneous applications in pending writ petitions on behalf of Shah Raiz Khan, son of Aleema Khan, and Sakeena Niazi, daughter of Noreen Niazi.The pleas challenged the denial of meetings between the detained women and their family members and lawyers, and also raised the issue of access to medicines.The families have alleged that neither relatives nor legal counsel have been permitted to meet the three women or provide them with medicines. The applications stated that medicines had been provided to the sisters on only one occasion and that no one had subsequently been allowed to meet them, Dawn reported.The pleas have sought directions from the Lahore High Court allowing family members and lawyers to meet the detained women and provide them with medicines, according to Dawn.Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of PTI's September 27 protest call.The detentions came amid a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its planned countrywide demonstrations and march to Islamabad. The party had called for the protests to demand Imran Khan's release and mobilise support for the supremacy of the Constitution.On September 24, the Lahore High Court had declined a request to immediately suspend notifications ordering the preventive detention of the three sisters.Imran Khan has been in Adiala Jail since August 2023. His detention and the PTI's protests have remained at the centre of a wider political confrontation in Pakistan, with the party continuing to demand his release.
Article Summary: Kasim Khan claims his three aunts remain 'abducted' by Pakistani authorities. He also says he and his brother have had no contact with their father for six months. His aunts Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned September 27 protest.

Article Title: Pak army chief Munir bypasses PM Sharif, moves to deploy more military assets to Saudi Arabia
Article Text:
Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is built on on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistani pact under which Pakistan had sent about 8,000 troops to the kingdom by May (Photo: Agencies).

Pakistan defence forces chief Asim Munir agreed to quickly deploy more Pakistani troops to Saudi Arabia , despite the Pakistani Parliament voting to stay out of the Houthi conflict 11 years ago.The Mecca defence pact signed by Pakistan with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August was invoked for the first time on Monday, amid increasing Houthi attacks on the Saudi kingdom.According to Reuters, the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is based on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistani pact under which Pakistan had sent about 8,000 troops to the kingdom by May.Pakistan's information ministry said the alliance "has gone through all necessary government procedures".However, it did not clarify if the cabinet or parliament was involved, calling details of the deployment "a matter ​of operational confidentiality."Senior fellow for South Asia at the Atlantic ​Council, Michael Kugelman, told Reuters that Pakistan is currently in a different era, with a comparatively weaker parliament."There were times in the past when Pakistan's parliament would vote not to send ⁠troops, and the military would abide by that decision. But it's a different era now," Kugelman said.Pakistan's armed forces have often been accused of holding the reins of Islamabad’s politics.In 2025, Munir was elected as the field marshal, the chief of all defence forces in Pakistan. Constitutional changes have allowed him to hold the position till 2030, with lifetime rank as the field marshal.Munir is also immune to any criminal prosecution, signalling the military's increasing influence over the constitutional establishment.Munir is widely acknowledged to be more powerful domestically than any of his predecessors. The military has control over major government portfolios like defence and foreign relations.Jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan ’s party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), currently protesting for his release, has accused the army of dominating politics.The relationship between Imran Khan and Asim Munir has reportedly been bitter since 2019, when Munir, then director-general of Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), was removed after less than eight months in the post, reportedly at the insistence of the then-PM Khan.No official reason was given for Munir’s removal.Khan was himself ousted as prime minister in April 2022. Seven months later, in November 2022, Munir returned to the centre of Pakistan’s power structure when PM Shehbaz Sharif appointed him army chief, succeeding Bajwa.
Article Summary: Pakistan's armed forces have often been accused of holding the reins of Islamabad’s politics. Mecca defence pact signed by Pakistan with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August was invoked for the first time on Monday. Pakistan's information ministry said the alliance "has gone through all necessary government procedures"

Article Title: Pakistan bets on electric vehicles as Middle East war sends petrol prices soaring 54%
Article Text:
Pakistan fuel prices to be revised every day

Poll Vote & Share your view How do rising oil prices influence your view on transitioning to electric vehicles? Strongly encourage me to switch Have no impact on my decision 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

EV sales accelerate amid fuel price pressure

Pakistan expects to achieve its electric-vehicle adoption target ahead of schedule as surging oil prices make the shift away from petrol-powered vehicles increasingly attractive, a senior government official said.The government aims for electric vehicles to account for 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030 under its EV policy announced last year. Haroon Akhtar, adviser to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on industries and production, said the sharp rise in fuel prices has reduced the time needed for buyers to recover the higher upfront cost of EVs.“I feel that the target we had set in our electric-vehicle policy last year, we will achieve it much earlier as rise in oil prices has brought cost recovery of EV to one to one and a half year,” Akhtar told Bloomberg in Islamabad.“People are realizing the benefit now. You don't have to pay for petrol,” he said.Petrol and diesel prices in Pakistan have risen 54% and 43%, respectively, since the Middle East conflict began in February, according to data available from Pakistan State Oil Company Ltd.Akhtar said sales of electric motorcycles and scooters have tripled from a year earlier, while electric-car sales have doubled, although industry-wide EV sales data is not publicly available.“This is an impact of the Middle East conflict, as fuel prices have gone up,” Akhtar said.Despite the growing incentive to switch to EVs, factors including high vehicle costs and limited charging infrastructure mean a large-scale transformation of Pakistan’s vehicle fleet and oil consumption will take years.The government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks. It is considering tax incentives for EVs to narrow the price gap between electric and conventional vehicles, Akhtar said.
Article Summary: Pakistan aims for electric vehicles to account for 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030. The sharp rise in fuel prices has reduced the time needed for buyers to recover the higher upfront cost of EVs. The government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks.

Article Title: Pakistan forces accused of quadcopter blast that killed 2 children in Balochistan
Article Text:
Pakistan forces accused of quadcopter link

A blast in Balochistan's Panjgur district killed two children and left three others injured, The Balochistan Post reported. The incident took place in Fateh Ali Bazaar in Gowargo tehsil, where the children had been playing.According to the report, the children noticed an unidentified object hanging from a tree. The object exploded after it was disturbed, killing two boys aged nine and 10. Three other boys, aged seven, nine and 12, were injured.The nature of the device that caused the explosion remains unclear.However, local sources alleged that it was connected to a quadcopter operated by Pakistani security forces. One source also claimed that explosives had been attached to a military quadcopter and placed in the area.The source further alleged that local journalists were later told to describe the incident as a hand-grenade blast or an explosion involving another device.The Panjgur incident comes amid other allegations of civilian casualties involving military drones and quadcopters in Balochistan.On September 24, four young men were killed and two others injured in an alleged military drone strike in Balicha, Kech, according to The Balochistan Post.Families of those killed said the men had gone there for a picnic and denied claims that they were militants.The incident triggered a boycott of courts across Makran, while lawyers called for an independent probe into the deaths.Earlier on September 18, five civilians were reportedly injured in alleged quadcopter attacks in Balochabad and Bullo in the Mand area, the report said.
Article Summary: Blast in Balochistan's Panjgur district killed two children and left three others injured. Local sources alleged that it was connected to a quadcopter operated by Pakistani security forces. Incident comes amid other allegations of civilian casualties involving military drones and quadcopters.

Article Title: Nearly 3 in 4 Pakistan inmates await trial amid prison overcrowding in country: Report
Article Text:
73% of Pakistan prisoners are under-trial, HRCP report finds

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the main cause of prison overcrowding in Pakistan? Delays in the justice system Arbitrary arrests Weak bail procedures Other reasons 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan's prisons are facing severe overcrowding, with people awaiting trial making up nearly three-fourths of the country's prison population, a Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) report has found.The report, 'Beyond the Prison Wall: Reducing Overcrowding in Pakistan's Prisons', said 73.41% of inmates were under-trial in 2024. The share has gone up from 66% in 2017, The Express Tribune reported.The report said Pakistan's prisons were operating at 152.2% of their approved capacity on average during July and August 2024.The HRCP said simply building more prisons would not address the problem. It pointed to delays in the justice system, including lengthy trials, weak bail procedures and the widespread use of pre-trial detention.Punjab faces an even bigger problem. According to official figures cited by the HRCP, 74,773 prisoners were held in 45 prisons across the province in September 2026. The sanctioned capacity was 39,204, meaning the prisons were operating at nearly 191% of capacity.Of the total inmates, 54,932 were awaiting trial.Punjab has added new prisons, barracks and other facilities over the years, but the report said the additional capacity has not matched the rise in the number of prisoners.The scale of the problem has grown majorly. Punjab province had 52,803 prisoners against a capacity of 21,527 in 2010. Overcrowding in the province stood at 173.6% in 2024, according to figures cited by The Express Tribune.The HRCP blamed arbitrary arrests, delays in investigations and lengthy prosecution for the growing number of people held without conviction.As a result, many accused people remain behind bars for months or even years while waiting for investigations and court proceedings to move forward, the report said.
Article Summary: 73.41% of inmates in Pakistan's prisons were under-trial in 2024. The share has gone up from 66% in 2017, according to a Human Rights Commission of Pakistan report. The HRCP said simply building more prisons would not address the problem. Delays in the justice system, arbitrary arrests and weak bail procedures were blamed.

Article Title: 'Come to your senses': What is Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif's condition for talks with Imran's party
Article Text:
Shehbaz’s talks offer fails to sway PTI as long march presses on

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think dialogue is the best way to resolve political disagreements? Yes, dialogue can help No, other steps are needed It depends on the situation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Imran Khan-led Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Tuesday questioned the seriousness of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s offer for talks, calling it "merely symbolic" and saying the government had taken no concrete step beyond extending the invitation, Pakistan Today reported.PTI spokesperson Gohar said the Shehbaz Sharif-led government had also prevented PTI leaders from meeting the party’s founder and former PM Imran Khan , for nearly a year.Speaking to reporters in Rawalpindi, he said the last such meeting took place in October last year, Geo News reported.His remarks came after Sharif asked PTI to halt its ongoing long march towards Islamabad as a condition for holding talks.At an event in Islamabad, the prime minister warned that protests and long marches could hurt Pakistan’s economy. "I urge you to come to your senses, end the long march and sit-in, and then we will sit with you," he said.The PTI-led march, meanwhile, continued towards Peshawar on Monday, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi calling on party supporters to join the mobilisation.Afridi addressed march participants after the convoy reached Kohat and thanked residents for their "magnificent welcome". He said the convoy would resume its journey towards Peshawar from University Chowk on Tuesday, The Express Tribune reported.Declaring his loyalty to Imran Khan, Afridi said, “I am a soldier of Imran Khan. Even if the whole world comes together, it cannot put a price on me." He also urged supporters to send a message that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa belongs to Imran Khan.The chief minister had started the march from Lakki Marwat on Sunday after negotiations between PTI and the federal government failed to settle differences over the planned protest.Those talks, led by national assembly speaker Ayaz Sadiq, ended on Saturday without an agreement.The Pakistan government had asked PTI to call off the march, while the opposition sought assurances that its leaders would be permitted to meet long-imprisoned Imran Khan.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif asked PTI to halt its long march towards Islamabad as a condition for holding talks. PTI spokesperson said government had taken no concrete step beyond extending invitation. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi called on supporters to join mobilisation.

Article Title: Pakistan successfully test-fires extended version of Fatah-4 cruise missile
Article Text:
Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch.

Pakistan successfully test-fired its homemade extended version of the ground-based Fatah-4 cruise missile on Tuesday.The cruise missile is capable of engaging long-range targets with high precision, the army said. PTI reported.In a statement, Pakistan Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the “weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.”According to the Pakistan army, the test validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability.Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch.President Asif Ali Zardari , Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif , Field Marshal Asim Munir, who serves as Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, and the services chiefs praised the successful test.Pakistan had previously carried out a successful test of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile in May.The base version of Fatah-4 reportedly has a range of up to 750 kilometres and can reportedly hit targets with a five-metre accuracy.The military confirmed the new variant has an extended range but did not clarify how far.Fatah-4 is a conventional cruise missile of Islamabad’s army rocket force command. It flies at an altitude of about 50 meters to evade air defences and avoid radar detection.
Article Summary: Pakistan successfully test-fired its homemade extended version of the ground- based Fatah-4 cruise missile on Tuesday. Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch. President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Asim Munir and the services chiefs praised the successful test.

Article Title: Another showdown brewing in Pakistan? Imran Khan supporters hit streets after talks fail
Article Text:
